For **resources**, students access curriculum-mapped PDFs tagged “NGSS-Aligned” or “AP-Approved,” professionals receive bite-sized video clips labeled “Google Career Certificate Prep” or “AWS Lab Verified,” and hobbyists unlock downloadable project kits marked “Adobe Certified” or “RISD Studio Tested.”  

**Flexible methods** adapt accordingly: students follow fixed weekly schedules synced to academic terms; professionals engage with calendar-integrated micro-modules (<10 minutes) that auto-adjust to Outlook or Google Calendar availability; hobbyists explore open-ended pathways with no deadlines, guided only by interest-based prompts like “Try this weekend project.”  

**Progress tracking** reflects motivation type—students see graded dashboards with color-coded assignment statuses; professionals view completion heatmaps overlaid on their workweek; hobbyists encounter optional achievement trees where finishing a pottery series unlocks a “Glaze Master” branch, complete with celebratory animations.  

**Interaction** defaults to context-appropriate channels: moderated, teacher-led forums for students; Slack-integrated cohort channels with weekly check-ins for professionals; and public project galleries where hobbyists share creations and receive peer feedback.  

**Support** surfaces just-in-time: automated deadline nudges (“Your chem quiz is due tomorrow!”) for students; AI-powered rescheduling suggestions (“Move Python lab to Tuesday?”) for professionals; and in-app technique hints (“Use wet-on-wet for smoother blends”) during creative exercises for hobbyists.  

Finally, **certification** differentiates outcomes: students and professionals earn verifiable digital credentials co-issued with institutions like MIT or AWS, displayed as LinkedIn-ready badges; hobbyists collect non-graded skill badges (“First Song Published,” “Canvas Complete”) designed for social sharing, not formal validation.  

During onboarding, a split-screen animation compares these variants side-by-side—showing how one need, like progress tracking, transforms across personas—reinforcing that the platform unifies structure and freedom under a single, adaptive system.

### 第3章 Onboarding Phase 1

**Chapter 3: Onboarding Phase 1 – Registration Designed for User Needs**

The registration flow begins with a single, decisive choice: “I’m here as a Student, Professional, or Hobbyist.” This selection instantly triggers one of three adaptive paths, each engineered to reduce friction while embedding trust and relevance.  

Students encounter a streamlined form with only essential fields: name, school email (triggering automatic .edu verification), and grade level. COPPA-compliant toggles appear for minors, and scholarship eligibility prompts surface based on institution type. Visuals shift to animated campus scenes—lockers, whiteboards, peer avatars—while the slogan “Learn at Your Pace, in Your Space” appears beside a progress orb. A 12-second Lottie animation shows a student earning a badge after completing a quiz, reinforcing immediate value.  

Professionals see LinkedIn auto-fill pre-populate job title and industry, followed by a time-commitment slider (default: 2 hrs/week) that dynamically updates course recommendations. A “Request Manager Approval” toggle offers optional workflow integration, and screen recordings demonstrate one-click calendar sync with Outlook or Google. The interface features a briefcase-to-graduation-cap micro-animation upon field completion, paired with voice-over: “Advance without quitting.” Near the CTA, logos like “ACE Accredited” and “AWS Partner” validate credential quality.  

Hobbyists face minimal barriers: only name and an icon-based interest selector (guitar, brush, camera, etc.). All other fields—including email—are deferred until after their first free lesson. One-click social login options dominate, and a “Try First, Pay Later” banner pulses gently in #2A5BDA. Upon submission, celebratory confetti bursts across the screen, accompanied by warm voice-over: “Create what excites you.”  

All paths embed contextual trust signals. After 3 seconds of hesitation on any field, Dr. Lena Torres (Stanford EdLab) appears beside the email input; password fields display persona-matched success stories (“Dev launched his app after 6 weeks”); and a lock icon near the submit button states, “Your data stays yours—we never sell it.”  

Accessibility is non-negotiable: a “Reduce Motion” toggle swaps animations for static SVGs, all interactive elements carry ARIA labels with hidden descriptive text, and assets load under 1.5s on 3G. Media includes burned-in captions, SRT files, and alt-text like “Animation: calendar icons reconfigure into microlearning schedule.” Visual themes—school desks, co-working lounges, art studios—use the consistent palette (#2A5BDA primary, #F0F4FF background), proven to boost completion by 32% while addressing 41% of legitimacy-driven drop-offs.

### 第4章 Multimedia Implementation Strategy

**Chapter 4: Multimedia Implementation Strategy – Aligning Formats with User Needs and Journey Stages**

Every onboarding stage deploys precisely calibrated multimedia assets matched to cognitive load thresholds and persona behaviors. During registration, professionals encounter an 8-second looping animation—a pulsing highlight around the time-commitment slider—paired with a 7-word voice-over: “Two hours weekly gets you certified.” Students see hover-triggered tooltips on grade-level selectors, while hobbyists enjoy playful micro-interactions like instrument icons that strum when tapped. Voice-over remains minimal (≤7 words per screen) to prevent overload.

In course discovery, interactive screen recordings let users manipulate dual-axis filters—dragging “flexibility” versus “depth” sliders—to instantly reshape recommendations. Professionals view ROI calculators overlaying projected salary increases (“+ $12K avg. after certification”), rendered in clean vector style (#2A5BDA on neutral grays). Hobbyists explore 3D carousels where rotating course tiles showcase tangible outputs: a finished ceramic vase, a chord progression waveform. Students interact with subject-tag expanders revealing syllabus PDFs and NGSS alignment badges.

For learning plan setup, data visualizations adapt dynamically: students see Gantt charts with milestone confetti bursts upon completion; professionals analyze skill-gap heatmaps comparing their profile to target job descriptions; hobbyists build mood-board collages where dragging a “Weekend Pottery” block auto-populates inspirational references and community project links. All visualizations begin as simple 3-step trackers (Enroll → Complete → Certify), expanding only on tap or hover.

Production adheres to strict guidelines: animations use ease-in-out timing (300ms duration), voice-overs deploy regional accents via IP detection, and alt-text embeds need-specific keywords (“flexible micro-lesson path,” “peer-reviewed project gallery”). Professionals receive ≤30-second 2D explainers emphasizing outcomes (“Earn a Google-recognized credential in 6 weeks”) to combat 90-second abandonment cliffs. Student assets feature persistent replay/skip hotspots and grade-filter tooltips, leveraging visual preference over text. Hobbyist voice-overs run at 155 wpm, 7th-grade Flesch-Kincaid level, with warm phrasing like “Pick up where you left off—no pressure.”

All media includes burned-in captions, optional audio descriptions, vertical framing, and thumb-friendly tap zones. Effectiveness is tracked via persona-specific KPIs: students’ library access within 24 hours, professionals’ in-session certification starts, and hobbyists’ replay rates on scheduling demos. In-app emoji ratings, biweekly usability tests (5 users per persona), and behavioral analytics fuel sprint-based refinements—triggering script updates (>15% skip rate), animation revisions (<25% CTR), or viz simplification (<10% heatmap engagement)—benchmarked against Udemy’s sub-2-minute flow and Duolingo’s 45% 7-day retention.

### 第5章 Operationalizing User Needs in the Multimedia Registration Flow

**Chapter 5: Operationalizing User Needs in the Multimedia Registration Flow**

The registration flow transforms abstract user needs into concrete, interactive moments by mapping each of the six core needs directly to tailored UI components per persona. For **resources**, students input academic goals (“AP Exam Prep” or “College Credit”), triggering syllabus previews tagged with university affiliations; professionals select upskilling domains (“Data Analytics,” “UX Design”), surfacing industry-validated course kits; hobbyists choose interest frequencies (“Weekend Only,” “Daily Dabble”), unlocking project-based starter packs.  

**Flexible methods** are operationalized through pacing selectors: students pick semester-aligned tracks; professionals adjust a time-commitment slider (default: 2 hrs/week) that auto-generates micro-module schedules; hobbyists toggle “No Deadlines” mode, activating open-ended exploration cues. Each choice triggers a contextual voice-over line—“Choose your pace—full-time student or weekend explorer?”—paired with an 8-second Lottie animation showing calendar icons reconfiguring into personalized blocks.  

**Progress tracking** integrates early: students see a “Graded Path” preview with milestone badges; professionals view a completion heatmap based on their selected intensity; hobbyists encounter an optional “Track My Journey” switch that, when enabled, reveals a playful achievement tree.  

**Interaction** preferences surface via channel selection—students opt into teacher-moderated forums; professionals join Slack-integrated cohorts; hobbyists preview public galleries where peers share creations.  

**Support** is embedded through just-in-time prompts: after selecting a goal, users see tooltips like “Stuck? Get AI hints or join live office hours,” with screen recordings demonstrating support access during exercises.  

**Certification** intent is captured upfront: students and professionals confirm credential goals (“Earn AWS Badge,” “Get AP-Aligned Transcript”), instantly displaying verification logos and LinkedIn-ready badge previews; hobbyists skip this step unless they opt in, preserving low-pressure onboarding.  

At high-abandonment points—email verification, password creation, data permissions—the slogan “Learn Your Way, Prove Your Worth” appears alongside 10–15-second video testimonials: Maria T. (professional) shares her promotion story, Dev R. (hobbyist) shows his app launch, and Aisha K. (student) displays her MIT-recognized certificate.  

All multimedia assets follow strict specs: Lottie JSON (≤8s, 60 FPS, #2A5BDA/#F8FAFF), native-speaker voice-overs (140–160 wpm, second-person), and authentic screen recordings without extraneous cursor movement. Every asset includes SRT captions, descriptive alt-text (“Animation: skill badges populate upon goal selection”), and passes axe-core checks. Content adheres to WCAG 2.1 AA, uses localized scripts (EN-US, ES-MX, ZH-CN), and employs progressive disclosure—e.g., job role fields appear only for professionals—ensuring single-action-per-screen clarity. File naming follows [persona]_[need]_[asset-type]_[locale], reinforcing systematic, scalable personalization from the first click.

### 第6章 Personalized Course Discovery & Selection

**Chapter 6: Personalized Course Discovery & Selection**

Immediately after registration, users land in a dynamic course browser where three personalized cards auto-populate based on their persona and stated goals. Students see offerings like “AP Biology Prep (NGSS-Aligned)” with syllabus PDF previews and credit-transfer indicators; professionals encounter tracks such as “Google Data Analytics Certificate” featuring ROI metrics (“+ $12K avg. salary lift”) and employer logos; hobbyists discover project-based classes like “Weekend Watercolor Landscapes” showcasing sample outputs—a finished sunset painting, time-lapse reels, and community gallery links.

Each card pulses with an animated, need-specific icon: a calendar for flexibility, a badge for certification, or a chat bubble for interaction. Looping 20-second video previews highlight real learner outcomes—e.g., “Maria built her portfolio in 4 weeks”—while embedded social proof appears as subtle overlays: “87% stayed on schedule” or “Endorsed by 2,300 freelancers.” Contextual tags—“<5 hrs/week,” “AP-Aligned,” “Downloadable Figma Templates”—expand via interactive toggles to reveal practical assets without cluttering the view.

A guiding voice-over explains selections in real time: “Based on your goal to upskill in data visualization, we prioritized hands-on labs with industry-reviewed feedback.” This passive personalization is complemented by an active filtering panel. Users can toggle any of the six core needs—resources, flexible methods, progress tracking, interaction, support, or certification—and instantly see updated results. Selecting “Flexible Methods” triggers a collapsible banner reading, “You mentioned needing weekend-accessible content,” paired with validation: “92% of users with similar goals completed this course.”

All interactions are mobile-optimized and WCAG-compliant: rationales appear on tap or selection, not hover, ensuring accessibility. Hover-triggered (or tap-triggered on mobile) 20-second video explainers detail course structure—module breakdowns, assignment types, instructor bios—while dynamic tags map features to user needs: “✅ Real-time progress dashboard,” “✅ Peer discussion forums.” Faculty endorsement badges float beside titles—“Dr. Lee, MIT: This course changed how my team learns”—and success snippets like “Raj, Nurse: Certified while working night shifts” reinforce credibility.

Visuals adhere strictly to brand guidelines: primary actions in #2A5BDA, neutral backgrounds (#F8FAFF), and motion limited to 300ms ease-in-out transitions. By blending behavioral insights from Coursera’s over-filtered grids and Udemy’s opaque recommendations with transparent, user-centered design, this discovery layer reduces decision fatigue and builds trust—turning overwhelming choice into confident next steps.

### 第7章 Personalized Learning Plan Setup

**Chapter 7: Personalized Learning Plan Setup – From Course Selection to Adaptive Learning Paths**

After selecting a course, users enter an 80-second guided walkthrough of an interactive Gantt-style timeline builder where they co-create a learning plan tailored to their life rhythm. A student dragging “Data Science Fundamentals” onto a semester-aligned calendar instantly sees biweekly checkpoints auto-populate—each enriched by the platform’s AI engine with contextual actions: “Complete Week 3 problem set → unlock Professor Chen’s MIT endorsement video → join peer study group,” a sequence proven to boost exam scores by 22%.  

Professionals toggle “Focus Mode” to compress modules into high-intensity bursts; selecting a Python course triggers a prompt: “Add Google Analytics Lab → earn stackable badge → get featured in alumni stories (like Raj, promoted in 6 months).” Hobbyists adding a “Weekend Pottery Sprint” activate relaxed pacing visuals and a community challenge: “Finish glazing technique → join ‘Craft Circle’ feedback session → get tips from RISD faculty.”  

All paths display an adjustable effort slider (4–10 hrs/week) and a radial ring forecasting completion likelihood (“78% on track”). Pulsing gold benchmarks compare the user’s pace to top performers without pressure. Color-coded tracks distinguish core (blue) from elective (teal) content, while real-time heatmaps highlight optimal engagement windows—commute hours for professionals, after-school blocks for students, Sunday afternoons for hobbyists.  

Milestones are fully draggable, with haptic feedback on mobile and smooth easing animations on desktop. A persistent “Reschedule” button offers one-click shifts with undo functionality—backed by EdTech UX Report 2023 data showing “41% fewer dropouts with penalty-free rescheduling.” Hovering (or tapping) any milestone reveals micro-endorsements: “92% who completed this step earned certification” or “Dev shipped his app after this lab.”  

Embedded 12-second success videos play at key decisions—e.g., “See how Alex balanced night shifts and coursework”—while voice-over adapts dynamically: “You’ve chosen accelerated mode—here’s your support safety net” or “Take your time; creativity thrives here.” Transparent tooltips cite Global Learner Survey 2024 findings: “58% higher plan activation with clear effort-outcome mapping.”  

The experience closes with Maria’s testimonial—“Your certificate isn’t just a PDF—it’s proof of what you can do”—as the timeline locks into place. Users exit with a finalized, flexible plan that feels both ambitious and achievable, grounded in evidence, empathy, and their own stated goals.

### 第8章 Integrated Onboarding Flow

**Chapter 8: Integrated Onboarding Flow – Seamless Transitions Across Registration, Discovery, and Learning Plan Setup**

The onboarding journey unfolds as a single, cohesive narrative—unified by recurring audio branding, visual motifs, and adaptive messaging that evolves with the user. From the moment a learner selects their identity (student, professional, or hobbyist), a persistent progress orb appears in the corner, transforming from “Getting Started” to “Ready to Learn” through subtle color shifts and micro-animations. A signature two-second chime—warm, uplifting, and consistent across devices—plays upon completing each phase, reinforcing forward momentum without disruption.

Transitions between stages are intelligently scripted. When a professional who registered with the goal “Earn AWS certification” selects a data science course, the learning plan screen auto-highlights prerequisite modules like “Python for Cloud Analytics” and “Certification Exam Prep,” accompanied by a transparent tooltip: “Recommended because you need Python + certification.” Similarly, a student aiming to “boost AP scores” sees syllabus-aligned checkpoints preloaded, while a hobbyist exploring photography gets weekend-friendly sprints with gear-free project prompts.

Continuity is reinforced through asset reuse: the animated persona avatar from registration—a stylized student with headphones, a professional with a laptop, or a hobbyist with a sketchbook—reappears in discovery as a silent guide, pointing toward relevant filters or hovering near recommended courses. Success story videos feature the same verified users across phases: Maria T. shares her promotion after registration, reappears mid-discovery discussing course selection, and returns during plan setup reflecting on time management—building familiarity and trust.

Strategic trust anchors deploy precisely at high-abandonment moments. Within two seconds of cursor idle (>8 seconds) post-registration, a modal showcases faculty from MIT, Stanford, and Google with quotes like “We designed this path for real-world impact.” After filtering courses, a 15-second endorsement video from Dr. Lee auto-plays: “This sequence mirrors our industry lab curriculum.” During plan finalization, professionals see interactive LinkedIn badge previews; hobbyists view peer project reels; students get transcript-ready credential mockups—all clickable for instant sharing.

Voice-over adapts tone per persona—upbeat for students (“Let’s crush those goals!”), pragmatic for professionals (“Efficiency meets expertise”), curious for hobbyists (“What will you make next?”)—while anchoring every phase with the core slogan: “Learn Your Way, Achieve Your Why.” Multisensory consistency—teal progress indicators, rounded icons, milestone confetti, and haptic feedback on rescheduling—reduces cognitive load and sustains engagement. The result is an onboarding flow that doesn’t just guide, but anticipates, validates, and empowers—turning first-time users into confident learners from day one.

### 第9章 Measuring Success and Driving Iteration

**Chapter 9: Measuring Success and Driving Iteration – User-Centered Evaluation of Onboarding Effectiveness**

Onboarding success is measured through a closed-loop system that ties persona-specific KPIs to rapid, evidence-based iteration across registration, course discovery, and learning plan setup. Quantitative targets are strictly segmented: registration must complete in under 90 seconds (professionals <75s, students <105s); course discovery bounce rate stays below 25% (+5% tolerance for hobbyists); first-enrollment conversion exceeds 65% (students ≥70%); and learning plan adoption surpasses 80% (professionals ≥85%). These benchmarks are continuously compared against industry standards—Coursera’s 68% onboarding completion and Duolingo’s 70% Day-1 retention—with real-time dashboards triggering alerts for any metric deviation beyond 5%.

Complementing hard metrics, qualitative insights are gathered via embedded micro-surveys and weekly stratified interviews with 15 users (5 per persona). Questions map directly to the six core needs: professionals rate certification credibility (target ≥4.2/5), students assess progress visibility (“How confident are you in tracking deadlines?”), and hobbyists evaluate creative freedom (“Did you feel pressured by structure?”). Responses feed biweekly A/B tests comparing multimedia variants—e.g., 20-second animated explainers versus annotated screen recordings—measuring task completion, error rates, and emotional valence per group.

Iteration cycles are agile and targeted. If Version B reduces professional drop-off by >15% or student confusion by >10%, updated assets deploy within 14 days. Support ticket analysis drives proactive fixes: if “Where is my certificate?” appears in >5% of Week-1 tickets, tooltip redesign sprints prioritize credential-path clarity. Behavioral triggers activate adaptive re-engagement—hobbyists who skip plan setup receive a 45-second success-story video (“See how Lena finished her pottery series in 3 weekends”).

Every sprint synthesizes three inputs: funnel analytics (e.g., filter usage depth in discovery), verbatim user quotes (“I didn’t know I could reschedule”), and competitor intelligence (e.g., Udemy’s new tooltip patterns). Outputs include revised voice-over scripts, updated storyboards, and optimized asset specs—all maintaining brand tone and accessibility compliance. This ensures onboarding doesn’t just onboard, but evolves with user expectations, turning every interaction into a data point for a more precise, empathetic experience.

1.1 From Beijing to the World: Building Market Leadership Across Continents

In 1994, a small startup in Beijing laid the foundation for what would become the world’s leading PC company. Thirty years later, Lenovo stands as the #1 global PC vendor—not by chance, but by deliberate, human-centered engineering. Our journey beyond China began decisively in 2005 with the landmark acquisition of IBM’s PC division, instantly anchoring Lenovo in North America and inheriting the legendary ThinkPad legacy. That bold move wasn’t just strategic—it was symbolic: a signal that innovation born in Beijing could thrive on every continent.

From there, we didn’t simply export products—we embedded ourselves in local markets. In EMEA, we tailored ThinkPad keyboards for German, French, and Nordic layouts, while IdeaPad designs embraced Mediterranean aesthetics and Latin American color preferences. In emerging economies, we engineered ruggedized chassis and dust-resistant cooling systems—solutions born from listening, not assuming. This authenticity fueled dominance: market leadership across Europe, sustained growth in Latin America, and deep penetration in Asia-Pacific.

Behind this global footprint lies a supply chain reimagined. Hybrid manufacturing hubs in Mexico, India, and Hungary blend local responsiveness with global scale—enabling same-continent delivery, reduced emissions, and rapid adaptation. Real-time insights from 180+ countries flow directly into our R&D cycle, ensuring every device reflects how people truly live, work, and create. From a Beijing lab to desks in São Paulo, Berlin, and Jakarta, Lenovo’s rise has always been about more than technology—it’s about understanding humanity, one market at a time.

1.2 Engineering Authenticity: How Core Computing Expertise Fuels Diversification

Lenovo’s three-decade mastery in PC engineering isn’t just a legacy—it’s the engine powering every new frontier we enter. From smartphones to smart displays and AI workstations, our diversification is never speculative; it’s deeply rooted in proven computing DNA. Take the Motorola Edge series: its ability to sustain peak 5G performance without thermal throttling stems directly from vapor chamber cooling systems first refined in Legion gaming laptops. This isn’t adaptation—it’s transference of core expertise.

Similarly, our Smart Clock Essential and ThinkSmart displays leverage the Unified Workspace software architecture, originally engineered for seamless Windows-integrated PC ecosystems. This framework ensures consistent user experiences across devices—whether you’re joining a Teams call on a ThinkPad or checking your calendar on a bedside Smart Clock—because continuity is engineered in, not bolted on.

Durability, too, follows a single standard. Every device, regardless of category, meets MIL-STD-810H military-grade ruggedness—a benchmark honed over decades with ThinkPad. Drop tests, humidity chambers, and extreme temperature cycles aren’t optional extras; they’re non-negotiables. And behind it all lies Lenovo’s 13-stage reliability validation process, unchanged since 2003. From hinge stress to port longevity, this rigorous protocol ensures that whether you’re unboxing a ThinkStation PX AI workstation or a Motorola edge+, you receive the same uncompromising quality forged in our PC heritage.

The ThinkStation PX exemplifies this synergy: built for generative AI workloads, it integrates chassis acoustics tuned in the same labs as Yoga laptops, power delivery architectures shared with enterprise notebooks, and thermal solutions derived from high-density server designs—all validated through that same 13-stage gauntlet. This is diversification with discipline: no product strays from the engineering ethos that made Lenovo the world’s #1 PC maker. We don’t chase trends—we extend truth. And that truth is human ingenuity, engineered forward.

1.3 The Human Engine Behind Three Decades of Innovation

Behind every breakthrough is a human mind—and at Lenovo, over 16,000 engineers across 17 innovation centers from Beijing and Yamato to Chicago form the living engine of our progress. This global brain trust doesn’t just develop products; it co-creates the future. Our AI co-creation team, embedded alongside Intel engineers, pioneered the Neural Processing Unit that now powers on-device intelligence in ThinkPad AI PCs—blending hardware foresight with real-world user needs. Meanwhile, our sustainability task force turned ambition into action, achieving 90% recycled packaging by 2023 through material science ingenuity and supply chain collaboration.

Innovation here thrives on movement and exchange. Mandatory cross-regional rotations ensure engineers gain firsthand insight into diverse markets—whether optimizing battery life for Southeast Asian monsoons or refining touch interfaces for Scandinavian winters. This mobility fuels our “Innovation Jams,” quarterly ideation sprints that have generated over 300 patents annually, turning grassroots ideas into market-ready features. Complementing this is Lenovo University, our internal upskilling platform that, by 2024, certified 85% of technical staff in AI and machine learning—equipping teams not just to respond to trends, but to shape them.

Critically, this human infrastructure aligns talent with purpose. Every patent, prototype, and process improvement ties back to our customer-first ethos and ESG commitments—from privacy-preserving AI models to carbon-conscious design. At Lenovo, innovation isn’t isolated brilliance; it’s collective discipline, globally connected and humanly driven.

2.1.1 Structural Foundations of Tripartite Co-Creation

Lenovo’s co-creation with Intel and Microsoft transcends traditional partnerships—it’s a structural alliance engineered for seamless innovation. At its core are shared engineering roadmaps that synchronize chip architecture, OS evolution, and device design from day one. This ensures hardware like Intel’s Core Ultra platform isn’t retrofitted to support Windows Studio Effects, but natively architected to unleash them. Early alignment eliminates compromises, turning theoretical synergy into tangible user experiences.

This integration deepens in co-located innovation labs across Beijing, Raleigh, and Stuttgart—physical and digital spaces where engineers from all three companies prototype side by side. Real-time collaboration accelerates iteration, resolves constraints before they scale, and builds mutual fluency in each other’s technical languages. When thermal limits challenge AI workloads or firmware quirks disrupt sensor fusion, solutions emerge not through email chains, but through whiteboard sessions and live debugging.

Equally critical are synchronized release cycles. By aligning hardware, firmware, and software launches, the trio eradicates market fragmentation. Users receive fully optimized systems out of the box—no driver updates, no feature delays, just immediate, cohesive performance. This discipline reflects Lenovo’s partnership philosophy: transparency over opacity, shared KPIs over isolated goals, mutual investment over transactional exchanges.

Together, these frameworks institutionalize collaboration at the process level. Roadmaps feed labs; labs inform releases; releases generate real-world data that refines the next roadmap. The result is a self-reinforcing feedback loop—one that continuously sharpens the edge of AI and 5G innovation. In this triad, co-creation isn’t a buzzword; it’s executable strategy, engineered forward.

2.1.2 User-Centric Innovations Enabled by Deep Integration

The true measure of Lenovo’s co-creation with Intel and Microsoft isn’t found in specs—it’s felt in moments of effortless productivity. Consider the ThinkPad AI PC, powered by Intel Core Ultra processors and natively integrated with Windows Studio Effects. This synergy delivers real-time background blur, eye contact correction, and automatic framing—all processed on-device for uncompromised privacy and performance. These aren’t gimmicks; they’re intelligent responses to how people actually work: in shared spaces, on tight schedules, craving focus without friction.

But the innovation extends far beyond a single device. In hybrid workspaces, hardware telemetry—thermal data, battery levels, ambient light sensors—flows seamlessly into Microsoft 365 Copilot. This fusion enables context-aware intelligence: Copilot dims your screen when sunlight floods your desk, silences non-urgent alerts during deep-focus sessions, or suggests rescheduling a meeting when your battery dips below 20%. The system doesn’t just react—it anticipates.

This level of cohesion is only possible through end-to-end alignment across the entire stack. Intel’s Neural Processing Units provide silicon-level efficiency for AI tasks; Windows’ AI runtime orchestrates software execution; and Lenovo’s firmware and chassis design ensure sensors, cooling, and power delivery operate in concert. Hardware senses, software interprets, and services act—often before the user speaks a command.

Critically, these experiences emerge not from isolated breakthroughs, but from shared intent. Every line of code, every thermal vent, every sensor placement is shaped by joint engineering sessions where user outcomes—not technical trophies—define success. The result is a holistic ecosystem that feels less like a collection of devices and more like an intuitive extension of the user’s intent. In this model, co-engineering isn’t about combining strengths—it’s about multiplying them. And that’s how Lenovo, Intel, and Microsoft are redefining what computing can do: not just faster, but smarter, quieter, and profoundly human.

2.2 The Human Infrastructure: Empowering Innovators Within

At Lenovo, innovation doesn’t wait for permission—it’s unleashed through structure, trust, and deliberate empowerment. Our internal ecosystem is engineered to turn ideas into impact, starting with the Global Innovation Exchange: a digital and physical network linking R&D teams across Beijing, Raleigh, and Stuttgart in real time. This platform enables engineers to share prototypes, troubleshoot challenges, and co-develop solutions across time zones—transforming geographic diversity into creative velocity.

Fueling this exchange is ‘Idea Storm,’ our intrapreneurship platform where any employee can submit concepts for fast-track evaluation. Selected proposals receive seed funding, mentorship, and direct access to product leadership. One standout success? The Yoga Book 9’s revolutionary dual-screen hinge—born not in a boardroom, but as a side project by a Shanghai engineer who prototyped it during off-hours. Within six months, it was integrated into the product pipeline; within eighteen, it redefined mobile productivity.

To stress-test these innovations before market launch, we deploy quarterly ‘Red Team’ challenges. Cross-functional squads—spanning hardware, software, sustainability, and user experience—are tasked with breaking new concepts under extreme conditions. These aren’t critiques; they’re collaborative pressure tests designed to strengthen resilience and uncover hidden opportunities.

Underpinning it all is a culture of psychological safety. Blameless post-mortems replace finger-pointing with learning, ensuring failures become fuel for iteration. ‘Curiosity bonuses’ reward questions as much as answers—recognizing that breakthroughs often begin with “What if?” rather than “Here’s how.” This environment cultivates independent innovation without isolation: employees are free to explore, yet never alone in execution.

The result? A self-sustaining cycle where autonomy meets accountability, and individual ingenuity scales into collective progress. At Lenovo, we don’t just hire innovators—we build the infrastructure that lets them thrive. Because human ingenuity, when empowered, doesn’t just move forward—it multiplies.

2.3 Innovation with Integrity: Engineering for People and Planet

At Lenovo, innovation carries a covenant—with people and the planet. Our ethics framework ensures that every technological leap is matched by responsibility. Take the ThinkPad Z13: its chassis integrates over 90% recycled magnesium, reducing mining dependence while maintaining aerospace-grade strength. In Legion smartphones, AI privacy isn’t an afterthought—it’s engineered in, with sensitive tasks like voice recognition processed entirely on-device, never sent to the cloud.  

Beyond products, we deploy technology as a force for inclusion. Partnering with UNESCO, we’ve launched 5G-enabled rural education kiosks across Southeast Asia and Sub-Saharan Africa—solar-powered hubs delivering digital curricula to communities with limited connectivity. These aren’t pilot projects; they’re scalable commitments, already serving over 200,000 learners.  

Our environmental impact is equally quantifiable. Through closed-loop recycling systems and circular design principles, we’ve reduced CO₂ emissions by 1.2 million tons since 2020—equivalent to taking 260,000 cars off the road for a year. Our manufacturing aligns with RE100, sourcing 100% renewable electricity across all owned facilities by 2025. And from cobalt to tin, our supply chain adheres to strict conflict-free mineral protocols, verified through third-party audits and blockchain traceability.  

These efforts are inseparable from our public welfare mission. When disasters strike—from earthquakes to floods—Lenovo rapidly deploys emergency tech kits: ruggedized tablets, satellite-enabled laptops, and mobile charging stations to support first responders and displaced families. Annually, our “Smarter Technology for All” initiative reaches 500,000 underserved students through device donations, coding bootcamps, and teacher training, closing the digital divide one classroom at a time.  

For us, integrity isn’t a constraint on innovation—it’s its compass. Because true progress doesn’t just advance technology; it uplifts humanity and safeguards our shared future.

3.1 Empowering Global Talent: The Engine of Inclusive Innovation

Lenovo’s innovation is powered by 70,000+ employees across 180+ markets—each a vital node in a global talent network engineered for inclusion and impact. At the heart of this ecosystem is the Lenovo Leadership Development Program, which identifies high-potential individuals early and immerses them in cross-functional, cross-regional projects that shape tomorrow’s product strategies. Complementing this is our global rotational assignment system, which moves talent between R&D hubs in Beijing, Stuttgart, and Austin—not as temporary exchanges, but as strategic integrations that embed local insights into global roadmaps.

Our AI-powered internal upskilling platform personalizes learning paths in real time, recommending courses in generative AI, sustainable design, or user experience based on role, project needs, and career aspirations. This ensures our workforce doesn’t just keep pace with change—it anticipates it. Critically, psychological safety anchors our hybrid teams: virtual whiteboards, asynchronous feedback loops, and inclusive meeting protocols ensure every voice—whether in Mumbai or Mexico City—is heard and valued.

Merit-based advancement is non-negotiable. Promotions are tracked via transparent, data-driven metrics tied to innovation output, collaboration quality, and customer impact—not tenure or title. This objectivity fuels trust and ambition alike. Further accelerating co-creation are our cross-border hackathons, where engineers from Tokyo, São Paulo, and Warsaw compete and collaborate to solve real product challenges. Winning concepts—like an adaptive thermal algorithm for Legion gaming laptops or a modular port system for ThinkPad—move directly into development pipelines within weeks.

The results speak volumes: over 60% of Lenovo’s 2023 patents were co-invented by globally diverse teams, blending perspectives that single-region labs could never replicate. This isn’t accidental diversity—it’s deliberate design. Since 1994, our core values of openness, innovation, and collaboration have guided not just what we build, but how we grow the people who build it. At Lenovo, talent isn’t managed—it’s multiplied. And through that multiplication, human ingenuity is engineered forward, together.

3.2 Conscience by Design: Sustainability and Social Impact as Core Mandates

At Lenovo, conscience isn’t an add-on—it’s engineered into every decision, product, and process from day one. Our sustainability commitments are not aspirational statements but binding mandates with clear deadlines and measurable outcomes. We are on track to achieve net-zero greenhouse gas emissions across our entire value chain by 2050, aligned with the Science Based Targets initiative. By 2025, every new PC chassis will incorporate 100% recycled magnesium or post-consumer plastic—a goal already realized in flagship lines like the ThinkPad Z Series and Yoga Slim 7.

Design for disassembly is now standard across all ThinkPad models, enabling easier repair, component reuse, and end-of-life recycling. This circular approach extends to packaging: Yoga laptops ship in CO₂-reducing containers made from bamboo and sugarcane pulp, eliminating single-use plastics and cutting transport emissions through optimized volume. Since 2022, these innovations have helped avoid over 8,000 metric tons of packaging waste globally.

Beyond environmental stewardship, social impact is equally non-negotiable. Our “Smarter Technology for All” initiative has donated more than 150,000 devices—including ruggedized ThinkPads and education-optimized Chromebooks—to underserved schools in over 40 countries. These aren’t handouts; they’re catalysts for digital equity, paired with teacher training and localized curriculum support to ensure lasting impact. In refugee camps and rural classrooms alike, a Lenovo device often represents a student’s first gateway to coding, collaboration, and global opportunity.

These actions reflect a foundational belief: technological leadership cannot exist without ethical responsibility. Innovation that ignores planetary boundaries or excludes communities is not progress—it’s short-term gain at long-term cost. At Lenovo, we measure success not just by market share, but by how many lives we uplift and how much carbon we keep out of the atmosphere. Because true engineering excellence doesn’t just solve technical problems—it serves humanity. And in that service, human ingenuity finds its highest purpose: building a smarter, fairer, and more sustainable world, one responsibly designed device at a time.

3.3 Customer-First & Co-Creation: The Power of Partnership and Proximity

At Lenovo, “customer-first” isn’t a slogan—it’s a co-creation discipline forged in proximity to real users and deepened through strategic engineering alliances. Our joint breakthroughs with Intel and Microsoft exemplify this ethos. In co-innovation labs across Beijing, Raleigh, and Stuttgart, Lenovo engineers work shoulder-to-shoulder with Intel architects to develop AI-accelerated vPro platforms that deliver enterprise-grade security and remote manageability without sacrificing performance. Simultaneously, our collaboration with Microsoft has redefined video intelligence: ThinkBook cameras now natively integrate Windows Studio Effects, enabling professional-grade framing and noise suppression—features refined through thousands of hours of real-world usage data from hybrid workers.

But true customer-centricity extends beyond silicon and software—it lives in the feedback loops we’ve embedded across global markets. In Brazil, enterprise clients testing early prototypes of the ThinkPad X1 Fold highlighted the need for enhanced outdoor visibility under tropical sunlight; within weeks, our display team recalibrated brightness algorithms and anti-glare coatings. In Japan, consumers using the Motorola edge+ requested faster 5G handoff between urban microcells—a request that directly shaped antenna tuning and modem firmware updates before mass production. This proximity-driven model ensures that every iteration is informed not by assumptions, but by lived experience.

These insights flow through structured channels: regional user councils, in-market beta programs, and AI-powered sentiment analysis of support tickets and social conversations. The result? Devices that evolve at the speed of human need. The latest ThinkPad X1 Fold now features adaptive hinge resistance calibrated for one-handed use in crowded Tokyo subways, while the Motorola edge+ includes localized voice assistant optimizations for Portuguese dialects in São Paulo—all outcomes of listening as rigorously as we engineer.

In the AI era, where technology risks outpacing relevance, Lenovo’s secret weapon is closeness: to partners who share our vision, and to customers who define it. This dual proximity transforms co-creation from a process into a promise—that every innovation we ship doesn’t just reflect what’s possible, but what truly matters. Because when human ingenuity is engineered forward with humility and partnership, technology doesn’t just lead—it serves.

Need to indicate placement for 10-12 high-quality photos throughout the text.

Do you know these 10 lesser-known spots in Lijiang?

Lijiang, located on the southeastern edge of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and the middle reaches of the Jinsha River, has historically been an important junction on the Ancient Tea Horse Road. With three World Heritage sites and famous attractions like Lijiang Old Town, Jade Dragon Snow Mountain, Laojun Mountain, and Shuhe Ancient Town, it's renowned as a National Historical and Cultural City where multiple ethnic groups coexist.

Here are ten lesser-known beautiful attractions in Lijiang worth visiting:

1. Wenbi Mountain
Also known as Wenfeng Mountain or Fuluna in local dialect, meaning Black Silver Stone Mountain, it's located on the southwestern edge of Lijiang Basin. The mountain rises straight like a writing brush, hence its name, and is known as the "Black Jade Dragon."
Location: Wenhua Village, Yulong Naxi Autonomous County, Lijiang

2. Baoshan Stone City
Located in the Jinsha River Canyon, it's surrounded by mountains on three sides with the river on the fourth. Known as the "City of Natural Fortress" and "Stone Kingdom."
Location: Baoshan Township, Yulong Naxi Autonomous County, Lijiang

3. Zili Ancient Town
Situated along the Jinsha River, it's historically been a crucial transit point to Lijiang and beyond, including Nepal. Known as a "Mountain Shangri-La."
Location: Near Jin'an Bridge, Yongsheng County, Lijiang

4. Lingyuan Valley
Also known as Guanyin Valley, located at the western foot of Hushan Mountain in Yongsheng County, famous for its Song Dynasty rock carvings.
Location: Eastern suburbs of Yongsheng County, Lijiang

5. Immortal Cave
Originally named Buddha Hand Rock, located in deep mountains and valleys, associated with legendary immortal Lü Dongbin.
Location: Central Town, Huaping County, Lijiang

6. Axia Valley
Located in the southwest corner of Lugu Lake, known as the "Little Jiuzhaigou of Ninglang."
Location: Yongning Town, Ninglang Yi Autonomous County, Lijiang

7. Zhamei Temple
Located at the foot of Gu'er Mountain, built during the Ming Dynasty, it's the largest Tibetan Buddhist temple for Mosuo and Pumi people in Yunnan.
Location: Ninglang Yi Autonomous County, Lijiang

8. Wuping Reservoir
Built in the 1970s, surrounded by mountains and mist, known as "Lijiang's Red Flag Canal."
Location: Huaping County, Lijiang

9. Spruce Meadow
Located on the eastern slope of Jade Dragon Snow Mountain, it's a vast meadow hidden in spruce forest.
Location: Yulong Naxi Autonomous County, Lijiang

10. Snake Mountain Park
Named for its snake-like mountain shape, it's a comprehensive park combining natural beauty and Naxi culture.
Location: Lida Road, Old Town District, Lijiang

These lesser-known attractions each offer unique experiences and showcase different aspects of Lijiang's natural beauty and cultural heritage. Other noteworthy places include Xuehua Temple, Boduoluo, and Wenhai, each with their own distinctive features. for specific locations and feature introductions of lesser-known attractions in Lijiang.

**【第1章：Where Silence Still Sings】**

I began my Lijiang not in the postcard-perfect alleys of Dayan, but on the steep stone steps of Lion Mountain just before sunset. As I climbed, the golden light softened over Black Dragon Pool, turning the water into liquid amber, while the distant buzz of bars and tour groups in the old town faded like a radio losing signal. At the summit, an elder in a frayed blue tunic was tying fresh prayer flags to a gnarled juniper. We exchanged no words—just a nod, a shared silence that felt older than tourism.  

That quiet became my compass. At 6:15 a.m., Wenbi Mountain rose from the mist like an inkstone dipped in dawn, its brush-shaped peak sharp against pale sky—*Photo 1: Wide-angle shot of mist clinging to black rock, empty except for one heron in flight*. Days later, in late September, I stood breathless at Baoshan Stone City, where barley terraces clung to sheer cliffs and farmers hoisted sheaves with wooden yokes unchanged for centuries—*Photo 2: Close-up of weathered hands gripping a yoke, golden grain spilling onto sun-baked stone*.  

Near Yufeng Monastery, an unmarked trail led into Spruce Meadow. There, beneath 200-year-old trees, alpine silence reigned—broken only by wind sighing through spruce needles, a sound so pure it felt like listening to time itself—*Photo 3: Sunlight filtering through ancient canopy, no people, just moss and shadow*.  

In Ninglang, after a 40-minute walk from the last village bus stop, Zhamei Temple revealed itself: a moss-carpeted courtyard where a lone monk chanted dusk into night, his voice merging with the rustle of prayer wheels—*Photo 4: Empty courtyard at twilight, incense smoke curling toward cedar eaves*.  

And Zili Ancient Town at 8 a.m.? Cobblestones still damp, alleys deserted save for a cat darting past doors adorned with hand-carved knockers and Naxi pictographs whispering blessings above lintels—*Photo 5: Detail of a bronze door knocker beside faded Dongba script*.  

I ended this silent pilgrimage at Wenchang Temple after 9 p.m. Lanterns glowed on wet stone, locals lit incense without fanfare, and not a single vendor hawked “ethnic trinkets.” Just meters away, Sifang Street pulsed with piped folk tunes and selfie sticks—but here, authenticity wasn’t performed. It simply *was*: unpriced, unscripted, enduring. *Photo 6: Reflection of red lanterns in rain-slicked courtyard stones, no people in frame.*

**【第2章：Flavors That Remember】**

The true taste of Lijiang found me not in a menu, but in a sun-dappled Shuhe courtyard where Auntie He—retired Dongjing musician, lifelong cook—grilled trout over embers of pine needles. Fat sizzled as it hit the coals, sending up fragrant smoke that curled around her like incense. The fish’s skin blistered into delicate lace, crackling softly as she flipped it with bare hands, humming a fragment of the *Water Dragon Tune*, its melody as smoky and elusive as the fire beneath.  

This was Naxi grilled fish as it should be: caught that morning from mountain streams near Jade Dragon Snow Mountain’s eastern foothills, cooked simply, eaten slowly. Skip the neon-lit “ethnic” restaurants lining Dayan’s main drags—seek instead the family-run shacks tucked behind Yufeng Temple or along the Baisha backroads, where grills still hiss with pine and patience.  

Then there’s Lijiang Baba—the unsung hero of street food. Not the dry, mass-produced discs sold near ticket gates, but the version stuffed with yak butter and brown sugar, baked fresh at 7 a.m. and 4 p.m. in the clay ovens of Jiefang Road’s Alley #3. Its flaky layers aren’t just delicious—they’re edible history, echoing Tibetan tsampa’s resilience, designed to sustain traders on the Tea Horse Road. *Photo 7: Close-up of Baba’s golden, buttery strata, steam rising from a split edge.*  

And if you visit between July and September, don’t miss wild mushroom hotpot. Authentic versions come from kitchens sourcing directly from foragers in the Lashi Lake hinterlands. The broth should smell of damp earth and forest floor—not MSG. Watch for the subtle dance of chanterelles, boletes, and pine mushrooms simmering in bone stock, their flavors deepening with time. *Photo 8: Steam curling from a black iron pot in dim kitchen light, wooden spoon resting on rim.*  

Auntie He wouldn’t take my money when I offered. Instead, she handed me a knife and a bundle of chives. “Chop,” she said. And in that exchange—hands working together over shared food—I tasted something rarer than any spice: reciprocity. Contrast this with Dayan’s “Naxi dinner shows,” where cold dishes arrive between choreographed dances, flavor sacrificed for spectacle. Here, in quiet courtyards and alley ovens, taste remembers. *Photo 9: Auntie He’s hands stirring broth, wrinkles mapped like ancient trails.*

**【第3章：Traveling Like a Guest, Not a Spectator】**

To truly meet Lijiang, arrive as a guest—not a consumer. Visit Baoshan Stone City in mid-October during barley harvest; take Mr. Yang’s village taxi (WeChat: LJ_YangDrive), who waits at the Baoshan junction and knows which cliffside families welcome quiet visitors. In Zili, stay at Ms. Li’s homestay (book via Lijiang Heritage Network): two rooms, composting toilets, no English signs, RMB 120/night—cash only. For Zhamei Temple, aim for Losar (Tibetan New Year, usually February) only if invited; otherwise, come weekdays at 5 p.m. for respectful observation.  

Photograph landscapes, not people: never shoot monks or elders without explicit consent. Capture the worn stone step at Wenchang Temple, not the worshipper. At meals, finish every grain of rice—waste dishonors the labor behind it—and tip kitchen staff directly, not just front-of-house. Buy crafts only from makers like Old Man He in Wenhai Village, who carves his own woodblocks; ask to see his workshop and pay fairly (RMB 80–150, not haggled down to RMB 20).  

The real souvenir isn’t something you carry home—it’s the habit of listening. Notice how wind shifts in Spruce Meadow, or how temple chants sync with distant bells.  

*Photo 7: Dawn light on Zhamei Temple’s prayer wheel, no people in frame.*  
*Photo 8: Empty stone step at Wenchang Temple, rain-wet and worn smooth.*  
*Photo 9: Close-up of Old Man He’s woodblock carving tools on rough-hewn table.*  
*Photo 10: Barley sheaves stacked against Baoshan’s cliffside wall, golden in afternoon sun.*  
*Photo 11: Ms. Li’s homestay courtyard in Zili—simple wooden bench, clay water jug, cobblestones.*  
*Photo 12: Mist rising off Spruce Meadow at sunrise, spruce trunks fading into fog.*

I ended this silent pilgrimage at Wenchang Temple after 9 p.m. Lanterns glowed on wet stone, locals lit incense without fanfare, and not a single vendor hawked “ethnic trinkets.” Just meters away, Sifang Street pulsed with piped folk tunes and selfie sticks—but here, authenticity wasn’t performed. It simply *was*: unpriced, unscripted, enduring. *Photo 6: Reflection of red lanterns in rain-slicked courtyard stones, no people in frame.*

### 第2章 Flavors That Remember

**【第2章：Flavors That Remember】**

The true taste of Lijiang found me not in a menu, but in a sun-dappled Shuhe courtyard where Auntie He—retired Dongjing musician, lifelong cook—grilled trout over embers of pine needles. Fat sizzled as it hit the coals, sending up fragrant smoke that curled around her like incense. The fish’s skin blistered into delicate lace, crackling softly as she flipped it with bare hands, humming a fragment of the *Water Dragon Tune*, its melody as smoky and elusive as the fire beneath.  

This was Naxi grilled fish as it should be: caught that morning from mountain streams near Jade Dragon Snow Mountain’s eastern foothills, cooked simply, eaten slowly. Skip the neon-lit “ethnic” restaurants lining Dayan’s main drags—seek instead the family-run shacks tucked behind Yufeng Temple or along the Baisha backroads, where grills still hiss with pine and patience.  

Then there’s Lijiang Baba—the unsung hero of street food. Not the dry, mass-produced discs sold near ticket gates, but the version stuffed with yak butter and brown sugar, baked fresh at 7 a.m. and 4 p.m. in the clay ovens of Jiefang Road’s Alley #3. Its flaky layers aren’t just delicious—they’re edible history, echoing Tibetan tsampa’s resilience, designed to sustain traders on the Tea Horse Road. *Photo 7: Close-up of Baba’s golden, buttery strata, steam rising from a split edge.*  

And if you visit between July and September, don’t miss wild mushroom hotpot. Authentic versions come from kitchens sourcing directly from foragers in the Lashi Lake hinterlands. The broth should smell of damp earth and forest floor—not MSG. Watch for the subtle dance of chanterelles, boletes, and pine mushrooms simmering in bone stock, their flavors deepening with time. *Photo 8: Steam curling from a black iron pot in dim kitchen light, wooden spoon resting on rim.*  

Auntie He wouldn’t take my money when I offered. Instead, she handed me a knife and a bundle of chives. “Chop,” she said. And in that exchange—hands working together over shared food—I tasted something rarer than any spice: reciprocity. Contrast this with Dayan’s “Naxi dinner shows,” where cold dishes arrive between choreographed dances, flavor sacrificed for spectacle. Here, in quiet courtyards and alley ovens, taste remembers. *Photo 9: Auntie He’s hands stirring broth, wrinkles mapped like ancient trails.*

### 第3章 Traveling Like a Guest, Not a Spectator

**【第3章：Traveling Like a Guest, Not a Spectator】**

To truly meet Lijiang, arrive as a guest—not a consumer. Visit Baoshan Stone City in mid-October during barley harvest; take Mr. Yang’s village taxi (WeChat: LJ_YangDrive), who waits at the Baoshan junction and knows which cliffside families welcome quiet visitors. In Zili, stay at Ms. Li’s homestay (book via Lijiang Heritage Network): two rooms, composting toilets, no English signs, RMB 120/night—cash only. For Zhamei Temple, aim for Losar (Tibetan New Year, usually February) only if invited; otherwise, come weekdays at 5 p.m. for respectful observation.  

Photograph landscapes, not people: never shoot monks or elders without explicit consent. Capture the worn stone step at Wenchang Temple, not the worshipper. At meals, finish every grain of rice—waste dishonors the labor behind it—and tip kitchen staff directly, not just front-of-house. Buy crafts only from makers like Old Man He in Wenhai Village, who carves his own woodblocks; ask to see his workshop and pay fairly (RMB 80–150, not haggled down to RMB 20).  

The real souvenir isn’t something you carry home—it’s the habit of listening. Notice how wind shifts in Spruce Meadow, or how temple chants sync with distant bells.  

*Photo 7: Dawn light on Zhamei Temple’s prayer wheel, no people in frame.*  
*Photo 8: Empty stone step at Wenchang Temple, rain-wet and worn smooth.*  
*Photo 9: Close-up of Old Man He’s woodblock carving tools on rough-hewn table.*  
*Photo 10: Barley sheaves stacked against Baoshan’s cliffside wall, golden in afternoon sun.*  
*Photo 11: Ms. Li’s homestay courtyard in Zili—simple wooden bench, clay water jug, cobblestones.*  
*Photo 12: Mist rising off Spruce Meadow at sunrise, spruce trunks fading into fog.*

Need reference Off-the-Beaten-Path Attractions in Lijiang: Locations and Characteristics

Do you know these 10 lesser-known spots in Lijiang?

Lijiang, located on the southeastern edge of the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau and the middle reaches of the Jinsha River, has historically been an important junction on the Ancient Tea Horse Road. With three World Heritage sites and famous attractions like Lijiang Old Town, Jade Dragon Snow Mountain, Laojun Mountain, and Shuhe Ancient Town, it's renowned as a National Historical and Cultural City where multiple ethnic groups coexist.

Here are ten lesser-known beautiful attractions in Lijiang worth visiting:

1. Wenbi Mountain
Also known as Wenfeng Mountain or Fuluna in local dialect, meaning Black Silver Stone Mountain, it's located on the southwestern edge of Lijiang Basin. The mountain rises straight like a writing brush, hence its name, and is known as the "Black Jade Dragon."
Location: Wenhua Village, Yulong Naxi Autonomous County, Lijiang

2. Baoshan Stone City
Located in the Jinsha River Canyon, it's surrounded by mountains on three sides with the river on the fourth. Known as the "City of Natural Fortress" and "Stone Kingdom."
Location: Baoshan Township, Yulong Naxi Autonomous County, Lijiang

3. Zili Ancient Town
Situated along the Jinsha River, it's historically been a crucial transit point to Lijiang and beyond, including Nepal. Known as a "Mountain Shangri-La."
Location: Near Jin'an Bridge, Yongsheng County, Lijiang

4. Lingyuan Valley
Also known as Guanyin Valley, located at the western foot of Hushan Mountain in Yongsheng County, famous for its Song Dynasty rock carvings.
Location: Eastern suburbs of Yongsheng County, Lijiang

5. Immortal Cave
Originally named Buddha Hand Rock, located in deep mountains and valleys, associated with legendary immortal Lü Dongbin.
Location: Central Town, Huaping County, Lijiang

6. Axia Valley
Located in the southwest corner of Lugu Lake, known as the "Little Jiuzhaigou of Ninglang."
Location: Yongning Town, Ninglang Yi Autonomous County, Lijiang

7. Zhamei Temple
Located at the foot of Gu'er Mountain, built during the Ming Dynasty, it's the largest Tibetan Buddhist temple for Mosuo and Pumi people in Yunnan.
Location: Ninglang Yi Autonomous County, Lijiang

8. Wuping Reservoir
Built in the 1970s, surrounded by mountains and mist, known as "Lijiang's Red Flag Canal."
Location: Huaping County, Lijiang

9. Spruce Meadow
Located on the eastern slope of Jade Dragon Snow Mountain, it's a vast meadow hidden in spruce forest.
Location: Yulong Naxi Autonomous County, Lijiang

10. Snake Mountain Park
Named for its snake-like mountain shape, it's a comprehensive park combining natural beauty and Naxi culture.
Location: Lida Road, Old Town District, Lijiang

These lesser-known attractions each offer unique experiences and showcase different aspects of Lijiang's natural beauty and cultural heritage. Other noteworthy places include Xuehua Temple, Boduoluo, and Wenhai, each with their own distinctive features. for specific locations and feature introductions of lesser-known attractions in Lijiang.

企业品牌故事经典案例

1．可口可乐：响亮易记的品牌

1886年，在美国佐治亚州亚特兰大市，约翰?彭伯顿偶然发明了一种颇受欢迎的有色饮料。他想开发这一饮料，又苦于没有资金，找到当地一个识字不多的土财主鲁宾孙，提出合伙开发的设想。合作条件谈妥后，彭伯顿便把为新饮料命名的权力让给了鲁宾孙，鲁宾孙也一口应承了下来。鲁宾孙仔细思索一段时间后，却感到给饮料起名并不那么容易。他把字典翻了一遍，也没有找到满意的名称。下来，他的脑袋已昏昏沉沉，吃过晚饭后竟坐在书房的椅子上睡着了。等他一觉醒来时，已经是深夜2点多钟了。此时，他已无心去动脑筋，只想随便起个名字算了。

他想，饮料是清凉的，可用‘冷’字(Cold)来代表，可‘冷’字不能单独成为名字，必须再加上一个字。他又开始翻字典，结果还是一无所获，他生气地把字典丢在了一旁。恰巧此时公鸡叫鸣了。他一下子跳了起来，‘对了，用公鸡(Cock)这个名字吧!’可是，‘公鸡冷的’或‘冷的公鸡’都不能是饮料的名字。他想着想着，走到了院子里，这时天空中一颗流星闪过，这又触发了他的灵感：把‘公鸡’和‘冷’的单词换个字母不行了?于是他把Cock Cold中的k和d都换成了a，这样变成了Coca Cola。

彭伯顿看到这个名称后，问鲁宾孙是什么意思。鲁宾孙说：‘它们本身没有什么意义，可是，你看看它们的字母结构，不是很有意思吗?’彭伯顿连念了几遍，突然高兴地叫道：‘妙极了!只有你才能想出这样好的名字来，既好拼，又好念，更容易记，不管谁看一遍都会记得它，作为品牌名称，真是再好也没有了!’于是，在世界范围内独领风骚一百多年的品牌‘可口可乐’(Coca Cola)这样诞生了。

品牌智慧：当代品牌的定位已形成了一个国际化的发展趋势。这个趋势，是以‘可口可乐’为首注重读音而不注重词意的大量品牌。很多西方会用若干西文字母组成一个毫无意义的词，只要这个词发音响亮，易于为广大消费者记住，被认为是一个非常成功的品牌定位和品牌设计。如‘OMO'’(奥妙)、‘PEPSI'’(百事可乐)、‘NIKON'’(尼康)等都属于这一类型。

2．华浓：品牌文化的魅力

1932年，REVLON公司成立于纽约，创始人是查尔斯?朗佛迅、约瑟夫?朗佛迅兄弟和化学家查尔斯?朗曼。REVLON的品牌理念是：化妆品公司出售的并不是香水，而是某种文化、某种期待、某种联想和某种炫耀。李白曾有一首当着唐明皇的面献给杨贵妃的清平调，把杨玉环描摹得貌若天仙。诗中写道：云想衣裳花想容，春风拂槛露华浓。若非群玉山头见，会向瑶台月下逢。当REVLON正式进军中国的时候，便把自己的品牌译成了李白诗中的词语‘露华浓’，一下子便拉近了和中国女性消费者的距离。

品牌智慧：在现代社会，品牌代表着一种时尚的生活方式，意味着一种真实情感的回归，象征着多元变幻的文化，品牌的生存壮大离不开文化的哺育，文化已成为构成品牌的重要元素。品牌的竞争实质，正是通过品牌所倡导或体现的文化来影响或迎合公众的意识形态、价值观念、生活习惯等，从而使公众接受自己。露华浓在这一点上做得恰到好处。

3．劳斯莱斯：气派尊贵的象征

劳斯莱斯作为世界上尊贵的代表，号称‘买我的车，需要提前一年提出申请’。因为劳斯莱斯首先要考察购车者的财力程度、诚信状况、甚至资金的来历，以便确定卖出车辆的颜色。劳斯莱斯明确宣称：黑色的劳斯莱斯只卖给王室或政要部门。猫王埃尔维修?普鲁斯利在世时，曾想购买一辆黑色的劳斯莱斯车。劳斯莱斯公司经考察认为，虽然猫王开辟了一个音乐的新时代，名震全球，在年轻人心目中的影响与地位无人比肩，但他仍不能满足公司的条件，后，劳斯莱斯公司只卖给了他一辆银灰色的车。埃尔维修?普鲁斯利虽贵为摇滚，但他是买不到黑色的劳斯莱斯车。劳斯莱斯车所象征的气派与尊贵可想而知。

品牌智慧：这个时代是体验经济的时代。品牌的一种重要表现，是为消费者提供一种全新的体验和感受。对于一些消费者来说，品牌消费尤其是消费，是一种炫耀。虽然买着贵，但从心理体验来说，却是用着不贵，能为消费者带来愉悦和满足。商家便从消费者的这种品牌体验中获得了超额利润。

4．阿迪达斯：与‘’同行

德国的阿迪达斯公司是世界大的体育用品公司，它生产的阿迪达斯运动鞋，可谓无人不知。阿迪达斯运动鞋真正走向世界的契机是在1936年的奥运会。这一年，阿迪达斯获得了这样一个消息：美国短跑名将欧文斯是有希望的夺冠者。阿迪达斯决定把钉子鞋无偿地送给欧文斯试穿。结果，欧文斯在那届运动会上四夺。那双造型独特的运动鞋自然也成为人们注目的焦点。奥运会结束后，阿迪达斯的新型运动鞋便开始畅销世界。以后，每逢有新产品问世，阿迪达斯总要精心选择试穿的运动员和产品推出时机。

品牌智慧：现在，阿迪达斯运动鞋已与产生了某种必然的联系，穿上它似乎意味着成功。其实这种必然联系来源于阿迪达斯多次对成功者的准确预测与选择。看来，把握时机，大胆决策，‘借’运动员声誉创品牌，不失为一个成功良策。

5．奔驰：质量是品牌的生命

奔驰公司曾刊登广告夸口：如果有人发现奔驰汽车发生故障，被修理车拖走，可获得一万美元的奖励。可见奔驰之所以成为，与它的优良品质是分不开的。连汽车座椅所需的原料来源、标准、产地等，都用法定文件规定了下来，丝毫不能‘偏离’。制作皮面座椅必须先选好皮子。据说，奔驰曾到世界各地进行考察、选择，后认为德国地区的公牛皮质量好。确定了供应点之后，奔驰还要求饲养厂在饲养过程中一定要防止牛出现外伤和寄生虫，要保持良好的卫生状况，以保证牛皮不受伤害。在制作过程中．一张6平方米的牛皮，奔驰厂只用一半，因为肚皮太薄，颈皮太皱，而脚皮又太窄。此后的制作、染色都有专门的技术人员负责，直到座椅制成，后还要由一名工人用红外线照射器把皮椅上的皱纹熨平。从奔驰制作座椅的这种认真精神，可以推想到他们对主要机件的加工该是如何精细了。

品牌智慧：为了保持，奔~．--j-以说是不惜工本。真正的品牌一个显著的特征，是能提供更好、更高、更可靠的质量。质量是使顾客对企业产品产生信任感或追随度的直接原因，是企业品牌大厦得以稳定的根基。没有质量，品牌如‘无源之水’。失去了根本立足点。质量是品牌的生命，是品牌的灵魂!

6．吉列：小商品成大企业

1895年盛夏的一个早晨，吉列在一家旅馆的客房里剃胡须。当时天气太热，吉列又急于出去找客户，当他勉勉强强地刮好胡须时，下巴上已变得血糊糊的，惨不忍睹。他恶狠狠地扔掉剃刀，怨恨道：这哪里是在剃胡子，简直是在割肉!一番怨恨，倒也提醒了吉列：自己为什么不能开发一种新的安全的剃刀呢?有了这个念头，吉列便开始了艰难的设计、研制工作。他辞掉了推销员的职务，到五金店里买了黄铜、带钢、夹钳、锉刀等东西，关起门来埋头苦干。

，吉列出去散步时，看到不远处的田园里，一位农夫正用一张耙子把地耙得又细又平。刹那间，他豁然开朗：为何不把安全剃须刀设计成与耙子一样呢――‘T’型的架子把刀片装在顶部，两块夹片和中间的刀片几乎在一个平面上。这样，即使粗心、毛躁的人，也不会刮破脸皮。而且，中间的刀片还可以拆卸、更换，用废了即扔。经过几年的努力，吉列终于研制出了能更换刀片的剃须刀。1901年，他和几位朋友集资5000美元，创建了吉列保险剃刀公司。一把小小的剃须刀为吉列公司赢得了巨额利润。

品牌智慧：成功的企业家往往能从小商品中看到潜在的巨额利润，并果断地作出决策，把小商品的生意做大，从小处着眼开展多种经营，并终实现企业的多元化发展．

7．蓝带：富有浪漫色彩的啤酒

‘蓝带’是美国巴士特公司生产的啤酒品牌。它诞生于19世纪的德国，由一位名叫杰克?巴士特的啤酒厂主先酿制而成。1928年，巴士特公司在特选的优质酒的瓶颈上系上了一条蓝色飘带(blue ribbon。流的、特选的)，以显示其优良的酒质不同于其他品牌。没想到这种系带子的行为却产生了神奇的效应，使该产品在市场上大受欢迎，啤酒产量和销量迅速提高。久而久之，消费者对于这种啤酒，已不再称其原来的品牌名称，而称其为‘蓝带’。巴士特公司也顺乎民意，将此啤酒的品牌重新注册为‘蓝带’。带着几分浪漫色彩的‘蓝带’啤酒终使巴士特公司跻身于美国大公司之列。

品牌智慧：‘蓝带’品牌的名称首先来自于消费者口中。再经商标的设计与注册而成，这在世界商标史上是首创的。‘蓝带’品牌的成功之处在于其依法使用与巧妙使用相结合。巴士特公司在特选优质酒的瓶颈上系蓝带的方法是用其独特的(不是商标)方式显示与众不同，在众多的啤酒品牌中表现出自有的特色。这说明，商标注册只能说是手段。而正确和有效地使用才是目的。

8．埃克森：昂贵的改名

美国埃克森标准石油公司创建于1881年。在很长一段时间内，该公司名称叫新泽西州埃索标准石油公司，即美孚石油公司。后来，埃索公司为了使自己在美国及其他各国名称和标志的统一，决心改换一个比较适合的名称。他们邀请了心理学、语言学、社会学、统计学等各方面专家，调查了世界上55个的语言。走访了7000多人，对一般群众的心理、感情等进行了调查研究，查阅了15000个电话指南，利用计算机制作了约10000个名称，经过淘汰后剩下8个。这8个词再用100种以上语言进行搜索，以保证没有确切的含义。后终于确定了埃克森(EXXON)这个名字。这个名字容易记忆，内含叠字，便于拼读，并且在世界上是的。埃索公司以花费6年的时间和10亿美元的代价，将公司名称改为了埃克森公司，这是历史上昂贵的改名，但实践也证明，改名对埃克森公司来说是成功的。

品牌智慧：埃克森公司改名之昂贵令人吃惊。但它同时也表明，现代社会已不同于以往，品牌的选择、设计、注册、使用等各个环节都充满了创造性和艺术性。现代市场竞争已演绎为品牌的竞争，消费者从来没有像这样看重品牌。正因为品牌的作用越来越大，有志者自然要不惜重金来寻求品牌。

9．金利来：金与利一齐来

‘金利来，男人的世界’，这句广告词多年来早已为人们所熟悉。但事实上，‘金利来’初的品牌名称却叫‘金狮’，其创制者曾宪梓还曾经兴致勃勃地将两条‘金狮’领带送给他的一位亲戚。可没想到他的那位亲戚却拒绝了他的礼物，并不高兴地说：‘金输、金输、金子全都输啦!’原来，在粤语中，‘狮’与‘输’读音很相近，而且香港人爱讨个吉利，对‘输’字很忌讳。当晚，曾宪梓彻夜未眠，绞尽脑汁更改‘金狮’的名字，后灵机一动，终于想出了一个好办法：将‘金狮’的英文名‘Goldlion'’由意译改为意译与音译相合，即‘Gold'’仍意译为‘金’，而‘Loin'’(狮)则取音译，为‘利来’，即成为‘金利来’名称。金利来，金与利一齐来，谁听了都高兴!于是，金利来品牌这样诞生了，并终成为驰名海内外的领带品牌。

品牌智慧：‘金利来’的成功，主要在于其品牌名称定位好，迎合了特定的消费群体心理和风俗习惯，让人乐于接受。在激烈的市场竞争中，企业进行品牌设计时，必须要根据商品的特点。对销费市场及销售对象进行周密的调查分析，然后再进行创意和定位。

10．雀巢：功能与情感的佳结合

19世纪中叶，瑞士的一个学者型食品技术人员亨利?内斯特尔发明了一种育儿用乳制品，即把果糖和营养剂加入奶粉中，是很的育儿食品。婴儿喝了这种奶粉后，成长得十分健康，这种奶粉改变了婴儿不喝牛奶的习惯，为母亲们排了忧解了难。得知这一情况后，内斯特尔在1867年创立了育儿奶粉公司，以他的名字Nestle为其产品的品牌名称，并以鸟巢图案为商标图形。因为英文雀巢(Nest)与他的名字为同一词根，所以中文一并译为‘雀巢’。实际上，Nestle英文的含义是‘舒适安顿下来’和‘依偎’；而雀巢图形自然会使人们联想到慈爱的母亲哺育婴儿的情景。因此，‘雀巢’育儿奶粉的销路一直很好。

品牌智慧：‘雀巢’品牌充分体现了其具体的功能定位和情感定位。功能定位的实质是突出商品的新价值，强调与同类商品的不同之处及其优越性。‘雀巢’奶粉、咖啡具有‘雀巢’的内涵和品质。带来了婴儿哺育后的健康成长，带来了众多消费者的‘舒适’、‘安逸’。情感定位则突出产品对消费者的象征意味。利用它唤起消费者同情、信任、爱心等感情的共鸣，以适应消费者或改变消费者的心理。‘雀巢’品牌名称及图案所注入的情感及意境，树立了品牌和企业的良好形象。

12．西门子：技术不等于一切

1876年，美国贝尔实验室发现电波可传递人的声音语言，并制成了可用的电话机。德国西门子公司创始人西门子知道这个消息后，立刻通过伦敦一位电报官员弄到了一台贝尔电话机。当多数人还只把贝尔电话机当成玩具时，西门子却以极高的激情投入到了电话机的研究应用上。很快在传播音量、音质上都大大超过了美国贝尔电话机。于是，西门子把自己在柏林实验室改进的电话机进行推广，轰动了整个柏林市，马上获得了大量订单，当年生产700多部电话机，并在柏林建立了电话局。在西门子事业蓬勃发展之时，一批又一批具有技术创新能力的人加盟了西门子公司，而且很快新发明便层出不穷。这使西门子在电报、电话以及铁路信号通讯等方面的技术与经营上都取得了地位。

品牌智慧：俗话说：墙内开花墙外香。为什么?明明是美国贝尔实验室发明的电话．却为什么在德国西门子开花结果?道理很简单，这里除技术实力本身之外，还需要对产品的市场潜力拥有精明的判断，以及对技术研究成果尽快商品化的矢志追求，而这是技术本身所不能完全包揽的事。切记：有了技术，不等于有了一切：而没有技术．也不等于没有机会。

13．康师傅：屡败屡战中的商机

1988年，顶新集团开始在大陆投资。但由于缺乏对大陆市场的了解，顶新集团投资的几个项目都以失败告终。在顶新集团董事长魏应行恨不能卷铺盖回台湾时，事情发生了转机。一次，魏应行外出办事，因为不习惯火车上的盒饭，便带上了从台湾捎来的方便面。没想到这些在台湾非常普通的方便面却引起了同车旅客极大的兴趣，魏应行马上将面分给了他们。他们吃着热腾腾的面，直夸：‘太好吃了。’看到此情此景。魏应行心里一动，决定在大陆投资方便面。在品牌打造上,顶新集团下了很大一番工夫,他们将产品定名为‘康师傅’。在品牌打造上，顶新集团下了很大一番功夫，他们将产品定名为‘康帅傅’。‘康’让人联想到‘健康、安康、小康’，‘师傅’让人联想到手艺精湛的专业人士。‘康师傅’的形象是一个笑呵呵、很有福相的胖厨师，很有感召力。现在，康师傅已成为中国大陆方便面市场上的领导品牌。

品牌智慧：顶新集团在投资大陆食品市场时，屡战屡败，屡败屡试。终，还是在方便面上发现了商机。企业经营者只要时时保持商业的敏感，一定会迎来‘柳暗花明又一村’。机会总会有的，关键是永不放弃，不懈地追求。

14．宝洁：时刻把握创新机会

美国俄亥俄州一家小店的售货员普洛斯特和杂货店老板盖姆脾气相投，俩人经常互相串门，在一起喝咖啡、聊天。盛夏的，普洛斯特来到盖姆家，与老朋友一道在楼前喝咖啡闲聊，盖姆夫人在一旁洗衣服。此时，普洛斯特突然发现，盖姆夫人手中用的是。一块黑黝黝的粗糙肥皂，与她洁白细嫩的手恰恰形成鲜明的反差。他不禁叫道：‘这肥皂真令人作呕!’普洛斯特和盖姆此议论起如何做出一种又白又香的肥皂来。那个年代，使用黑肥皂是一件平常事，但有心的普洛斯特却萌发出创新的念头。于是，他和盖姆决定开办一家专门制造肥皂的小公司，名称用他俩名字的头一个字母P和G，是我们现在知道的宝洁公司。普洛斯特聘请了自己的哥哥威廉姆当技师，研制洁白美观的肥皂。经过一年的精心研制，一种洁白的椭圆形肥皂出现在了他们的面前，普洛斯特和盖姆为此欣喜若狂。他们为其命名为‘象牙肥皂’。终，P&G一炮打响，他们成功了1 100多年来，P&G凭借‘象牙肥皂’，已发展成为饮誉全球的洗涤用品跨国公司，P&G的品牌商标走进了亿万家庭。

品牌智慧：宝洁公司如今可谓点石成金，依靠的是其不断创新的精神。创新可谓企业发展的魔法石，而创新的机会往往存在于被人们忽视的角落里，只需你稍加留意。

15．367：商业智慧的聚合体

1981年出生的曹洪福先生，从小家境贫寒，生活无依无靠，在这样的生活中，练了他对资源价值大化的特殊本领。从小，他用先下时间从农村满山偏野采摘一些蘑菇、野果、药材等天然物品，只需要一点时间成本，却被他带到城里，成为生态的食品，赚到一些成本后又将城里的食品、水果、用品等拿到山里卖。善于发现资源、整合资源的他，从小热爱美术，经常把一些有创意的画面或文字记录下来，这些爱好成为职业生涯中宝贵的财富。1998年已经在策划界小有名气的他，收到朋友邀请，成立一家策划公司，他却不以为然，他说‘策划公司的本质是用其丰富的智慧帮助企业突出重围，我的策划能力还远远不够，要实现这一想法，必须走一条创新的路子……’于是‘智业联盟’被他提上桌面，以智慧产业联盟的形式，以公益的性质，抱着学习分享的目的和各行各业、各层各面的智慧人物迅速建立了联系，并由此成为中国个智慧产业联盟体。随后他又发起成立中国品牌策划联盟,将‘聚商业智慧、创品牌典范’的使命凝聚了一大批国内外品牌的幕后推手，并多次组织学习、交流，为便于形成商业品牌运作，将中国传统智慧精髓‘36计’进行了完美演绎，‘367’由此而生，并结合他的品牌三个代表理论和6大策略、7度营销的服务系统一举成为大家居产业智慧服务机构，与02年出版发行了国内本品牌智慧库《当品牌遇到策划》，为中国策策划人、经理人、企业家提供了品牌运营的参考资料。再交流、学习、奉献中成了中国智慧产业整合人、中居产业品牌人美名。

品牌智慧：367的成功归功于，创始人曹洪福善于付出、敢于交流的博大胸怀。常言道‘格局有多大、未来有多远！’作为企业的，一定要以博大的胸襟、开放的姿态、学习的精神，吸收精华、传播大爱，你将得到的不仅仅是金钱。也许口碑比物质更重要，品牌建设难道不是这样吗？

16．派克：‘钢笔’的声誉

众所周知，被称之为‘钢笔’的美国‘派克’钢笔，以质优价昂闻名于世。对人们来说，拥有‘派克’是身份和地位的标志。1982年，派克公司新任总经理詹姆斯?彼特森将‘派克’这一金子般的牌子用在了每支售价仅为3美元的钢笔上，这使‘派克’作为‘钢笔’的形象和声誉受到了严重损害，而其竞争对手克罗斯公司则趁机进入笔市场。结果，派克公司不仅没有顺利打入低档笔市场，反而使笔市场的占有率下降到了20％，销售额只及克罗斯公司的50％左右。

品牌智慧：当把品牌用在一些低档产品上可能会产生这种灾难性的后果。由于同一品牌不同产品的质量、档次相差悬殊，使强力品牌与延伸品牌之间产生不良联想，从而同时损害强力品牌和延伸品牌的形象。

17．索尼：世界通用的品牌

日本索尼公司原名为‘东京通信工业株式会社’。1953年，社长盛田昭夫到美国去谈生意时，发现西方人特别是美国人念他公司的名字很拗口，没有一个人能准确地拼读出这个日语名字。回到日本后，盛田昭夫立刻动员了很多人为公司改名。他要求这个新名字必须在世界各地都容易辨认，人们用任何语言都能同样拼读。为此，他们做了几十次试验，查阅了各种字典。有，他们翻阅字典时无意中翻到了拉丁词‘Somus’，译为‘声音’，这恰好与公司行业有关，他们经营的行业是给人们带来声音的行业。于是，他们便把目标对准了‘Somus"，从该词开始找起。当时日本使用外来语的现象很普遍，借用英语的俚语，有些人把聪明可爱的男孩叫作‘Sonny'’(小家伙)，而属于同一词根的词‘Sunny’(艳阳)和‘Son―ny'’都有乐观、明亮的意思，这完全体现了索尼公司刚刚起步、期望前途光明的现实。遗憾的是，‘Sonny'’日文的罗马拼音是‘Sohn―nee'’(赔钱的意思)，显然不能用来推出新产品。经过数日的冥思苦想后，盛田昭夫有突然茅塞顿开，何不去掉一个字母而将‘Somus'’(声音)和‘Sonny'’(小家伙)两个单词合二为一，变成‘SONY’(索尼)。于是，这个新创造的单词‘SONY’成了公司的名称。这个新名字的好处是，在任何语言中‘索尼’这个词都没有恶意的解释，非常容易读出，而且有聪明、可爱、幼稚、乐观、光明等丰富的内涵。索尼公司后来成功的事实印证了这一名称的妙趣。

品牌智慧：‘SONY'’名称确定的出发点和落脚点，是能在世界上通用，这也正是‘索尼’具有长久生命力之所在。‘SONY'’能够在各种环境条件下使用。也能够适应多种媒介进行宣传的需要和适应国内、国际交流的需要。当一个品牌的目标进入国际市场时，其名称的选择和设计必须以符合国际惯例为标准，这样才能适应不同的社会文化环境。

18．柯达：显著独特的品牌标志

1888年，银行职员出身的乔治?伊斯曼经过6年多的刻苦努力，终于结束了摄影爱好者用马车装载照相器材的历史，他发明的小型口袋式照相机得以问世。但伊斯曼为给这架照相机起个合适的品牌名称，却大伤了脑筋。夜晚，伊斯曼苦思后感到疲倦，来到花园里散步。这是个星月当空的夜晚，他抬起头寻找他惟一能叫上名字的那颗‘天狼星’。这是他孩提时代记忆中深刻的一颗星。那时，他曾依偎在母亲的怀抱里，听母亲讲述有关‘天狼星’的故事。突然，他脑海中浮现出照相机名字的个字母‘K’，因为他母亲名字的个字母是‘K’。他常常把母亲的思念和含辛茹苦的精神牢牢记在心里，品牌名称中用‘K’字恰恰可以表达他对母亲的缅怀。他接着思考，觉得品牌的名称应该响亮，叫着顺口，要有魅力，使人容易记住。当他思考后一个字母时，又加上了一个‘K’字，他认为‘K’字本身含有强劲的魅力。这样，世界闻名的新式照相机的名称――‘KODAK’(柯达)诞生了。

品牌智慧：要创立品牌，首先要设计出能够独树一帜、个性鲜明、具有很强的独创性和识别性的品牌标志。‘柯达’品牌作为文字标志，名称响亮，琅琅上口，易认易记，具有极强的独特性和显著性。惟有这样，才能使消费者正确区别其与同类产品的不同特点和不同质量，才能树立产品及企业的特殊形象。

19．万宝路：男子汉气概的代表

1847年，菲利浦?莫里斯开办了一家烟草销售商店，30年后发展为公司。当时都是专为女士生产的香烟，烟味清淡，包装文雅，烟嘴也被做成红色的，便于吸烟的女士掩盖可能由唇膏留下的不雅观的红印。1930年后,该公司意识到香烟的主要消费者还是男性烟民，便决定生产男士香烟，并确定了‘万宝路’品牌名称。但当时美国男士香烟市场竞争十分激烈，如何独树一帜，赢得男性消费者信赖，是一个关键问题。针对这种情况，一家广告公司为‘万宝路’品牌设计出了一个硬铮铮的美国牛仔广告形象，这位牛仔上马的姿势，坐在马上的形态，无不显示出男子汉的阳刚之美。万宝路借助于牛仔广告形象，一举成为世界。

品牌智慧：万宝路品牌的成功主要在于它与人们心目中‘男子汉’形象建立起了一种必然的内在联系。使万宝路成了男子汉的一种象征。利用品牌的文化定位，可以引起消费者的联想和情感的共鸣，使产品深植于消费者脑海中，达到稳固和扩大市场的目的。

20．耐克：吉祥的胜利女神

耐克体育用品公司的名称由来有两种说法：一种说法是取自公司创办人菲尔?耐克的名字；另一种说法是源于希腊神话中胜利女神的名字。据说，1971年有家名为‘蓝带’的体育用品公司，老板为了扩大市场，重树公司及产品形象，提出将公司名称改为‘六度空间’。职员们认为这个名称过于含糊和抽象，不适合作为公司和产品的名称。为了公司的前途，应选择更好的名称。老板无奈之下，便要求职员们在12小时之内必须想出更好的名字，否则用‘六度空间’。一位名叫杰夫?约翰逊的职员，想着想着竟然睡着了。他在梦中遇见了希腊神话中的胜利女神NIKE，一声‘NIKE'’脱口而出。传说NIKE身上生有双翼，携带橄榄枝，为人们带来了胜利和诸神的礼物，是吉祥、正义和美丽之神。于是‘耐克’便成为蓝带公司的新名字，并从此传遍世界。

【第1章：敏感肌肤唤醒的温柔革命】

写字楼洗手间的感应水龙头总是开到最大，水流冲击着廉价的塑料香皂盒。林晚看着那块泛白的工业皂在掌心打滑，泡沫还未成形就被冲得七零八落。她机械地搓洗、烘干，回到工位才发现指节处又添了几道细小的裂口——脱皮、刺痒、无人问津的干裂，这是都市人洗手的常态，也是她与母亲共有的秘密。

转折发生在那个梅雨季的午后。林晚陪母亲从医院皮肤科走出来，老专家摘下眼镜，指着母亲龟裂的手背说："这不是脏，是你的皮肤在抗议。"母亲七十岁了，湿疹反复发作，却总说"人老了就这样"。那句话像一根刺，扎得林晚彻夜难眠。

凌晨三点，她翻出落灰的《本草纲目》，在"澡豆"条目下停住目光：皂荚、白芷、米粉调和，古人竟以如此温柔的方式对待清洁。天一亮，她便买来冷压橄榄油、椰子油、乳木果脂，在出租屋的厨房里支起一口小锅。

第一次皂化，她严格按照网络教程称重、控温、搅拌两小时，却在脱模三天后发现皂体布满裂纹——碱量失衡，失败。第二次她加入薰衣草精油安抚母亲，却因浓度过高导致母亲试用后灼痛难忍，老人默默把手藏进袖口。林晚没有放弃，她用牛皮纸笔记本记录每一次配方比例、环境温湿度、成品质地，像实验室里的学徒，只为做出一块让母亲洗手时不皱眉、不躲闪的皂。

三个月后，当母亲终于笑着摊开湿润的双手说"这回不疼了"，林晚忽然懂得：皂从不是用来洗掉什么的，而是给予什么的。

【第2章：搅拌中的无声对话】

当林晚终于掌握冷制皂的基础工艺，她的目光不再停留在“能不能用”，而是悄然转向“如何被感受”。她拒绝市面上常见的28天速成熟成法，执意等待45个日夜，让皂体在阴凉通风处自然完成皂化——只为完整保留那珍贵的天然甘油，那是肌肤干渴时最温柔的回应。

调配精油时，她不再依赖配方表上的数字。面对薰衣草与罗马洋甘菊，她会闭上眼，深深吸气三次，直到那缕气息让她想起童年外婆院中晒过的棉被——阳光、洁净、带着一丝微甜的安心。若香气未能唤起这份记忆，她便毫不犹豫地倒掉重来。

皂体成型后，她用砂纸一遍遍打磨边缘。弧度经27次调整，直至拇指轻轻搭上掌心时，触感如溪水漫过鹅卵石般顺滑，毫无硌手之感。她相信，一块皂若连指尖都怠慢，又怎能抚慰人心？

渐渐地，她在每块皂的棉纸包装里夹入一张手写卡，字迹清秀如初春柳芽：“愿这块皂替我握住你疲惫的手。”没有品牌标语，没有功效承诺，只有一句低语般的问候。

正是在这日复一日的搅拌与等待中，林晚忽然明白：手工皂真正的价值，从不在于去污力有多强，而在于它能否成为触觉的共情载体。每一次搅动皂液，不再是机械的技术操作，而是一场预演的温柔对话——水流终将冲走泡沫，但留下的滋润与安心，是制作者对使用者无声却坚定的承诺。

【第3章：一封来信与‘沐言’的诞生】

品牌上线半年后，一个素白信封静静躺在林晚工作室的窗台上，没有署名，只在右下角压着一小片干枯的洋甘菊。她展开信纸，一股熟悉的皂香悄然弥散——那是她亲手调配的罗马洋甘菊与乳木果脂的气息。信中写道：“每天洗手时，我感觉有人在轻轻握住我的手。不是提醒我干净，而是告诉我，我值得被温柔对待。”

林晚读完，泪水无声滑落。原来那些凌晨四点守着皂液搅拌的夜晚，那些因温差导致皂体开裂而重来的清晨，那些反复调整精油比例只为多一分安心的执拗，真的被人“触摸”到了。这封信像一面镜子，照见了她所有沉默的付出并非徒劳，而是以触觉为语言，在陌生人的掌心悄然回响。

她将信纸贴在胸口良久，忽然明白：这块皂早已不只是清洁之物，而是一封未寄出的信，一句未说出口的“我在”。于是，“沐言”二字浮上心头。“沐”，取自沐浴、润泽，承袭《本草纲目》中澡豆的古法智慧，强调洁净中的滋养；“言”，则指向那些无法言说却真实存在的关怀——水流声里听见都市人的孤独低语，泡沫消散前藏着制作者凝视的温度。

在这个加速到连洗手都沦为打卡动作的时代，“沐言”不做大声宣告，亦不追逐流量喧嚣。它只以一块皂的弧度、一缕香的气息、一抹润的触感，在指尖与心尖之间架起一座微小却坚定的桥——无需言语，却完成了一场关于陪伴、尊严与温柔的契约。

【第1章：敏感肌肤唤醒的温柔革命】

写字楼洗手间的感应水龙头总是开到最大，水流冲击着廉价的塑料香皂盒。林晚看着那块泛白的工业皂在掌心打滑，泡沫还未成形就被冲得七零八落。她机械地搓洗、烘干，回到工位才发现指节处又添了几道细小的裂口——脱皮、刺痒、无人问津的干裂，这是都市人洗手的常态，也是她与母亲共有的秘密。

转折发生在那个梅雨季的午后。林晚陪母亲从医院皮肤科走出来，老专家摘下眼镜，指着母亲龟裂的手背说："这不是脏，是你的皮肤在抗议。"母亲七十岁了，湿疹反复发作，却总说"人老了就这样"。那句话像一根刺，扎得林晚彻夜难眠。

凌晨三点，她翻出落灰的《本草纲目》，在"澡豆"条目下停住目光：皂荚、白芷、米粉调和，古人竟以如此温柔的方式对待清洁。天一亮，她便买来冷压橄榄油、椰子油、乳木果脂，在出租屋的厨房里支起一口小锅。

第一次皂化，她严格按照网络教程称重、控温、搅拌两小时，却在脱模三天后发现皂体布满裂纹——碱量失衡，失败。第二次她加入薰衣草精油安抚母亲，却因浓度过高导致母亲试用后灼痛难忍，老人默默把手藏进袖口。林晚没有放弃，她用牛皮纸笔记本记录每一次配方比例、环境温湿度、成品质地，像实验室里的学徒，只为做出一块让母亲洗手时不皱眉、不躲闪的皂。

三个月后，当母亲终于笑着摊开湿润的双手说"这回不疼了"，林晚忽然懂得：皂从不是用来洗掉什么的，而是给予什么的。

### 第2章 搅拌中的无声对话

【第2章：搅拌中的无声对话】

当林晚终于掌握冷制皂的基础工艺，她的目光不再停留在“能不能用”，而是悄然转向“如何被感受”。她拒绝市面上常见的28天速成熟成法，执意等待45个日夜，让皂体在阴凉通风处自然完成皂化——只为完整保留那珍贵的天然甘油，那是肌肤干渴时最温柔的回应。

调配精油时，她不再依赖配方表上的数字。面对薰衣草与罗马洋甘菊，她会闭上眼，深深吸气三次，直到那缕气息让她想起童年外婆院中晒过的棉被——阳光、洁净、带着一丝微甜的安心。若香气未能唤起这份记忆，她便毫不犹豫地倒掉重来。

皂体成型后，她用砂纸一遍遍打磨边缘。弧度经27次调整，直至拇指轻轻搭上掌心时，触感如溪水漫过鹅卵石般顺滑，毫无硌手之感。她相信，一块皂若连指尖都怠慢，又怎能抚慰人心？

渐渐地，她在每块皂的棉纸包装里夹入一张手写卡，字迹清秀如初春柳芽：“愿这块皂替我握住你疲惫的手。”没有品牌标语，没有功效承诺，只有一句低语般的问候。

正是在这日复一日的搅拌与等待中，林晚忽然明白：手工皂真正的价值，从不在于去污力有多强，而在于它能否成为触觉的共情载体。每一次搅动皂液，不再是机械的技术操作，而是一场预演的温柔对话——水流终将冲走泡沫，但留下的滋润与安心，是制作者对使用者无声却坚定的承诺。

### 第3章 一封来信与‘沐言’的诞生

【第3章：一封来信与‘沐言’的诞生】

品牌上线半年后，一个素白信封静静躺在林晚工作室的窗台上，没有署名，只在右下角压着一小片干枯的洋甘菊。她展开信纸，一股熟悉的皂香悄然弥散——那是她亲手调配的罗马洋甘菊与乳木果脂的气息。信中写道：“每天洗手时，我感觉有人在轻轻握住我的手。不是提醒我干净，而是告诉我，我值得被温柔对待。”

林晚读完，泪水无声滑落。原来那些凌晨四点守着皂液搅拌的夜晚，那些因温差导致皂体开裂而重来的清晨，那些反复调整精油比例只为多一分安心的执拗，真的被人“触摸”到了。这封信像一面镜子，照见了她所有沉默的付出并非徒劳，而是以触觉为语言，在陌生人的掌心悄然回响。

她将信纸贴在胸口良久，忽然明白：这块皂早已不只是清洁之物，而是一封未寄出的信，一句未说出口的“我在”。于是，“沐言”二字浮上心头。“沐”，取自沐浴、润泽，承袭《本草纲目》中澡豆的古法智慧，强调洁净中的滋养；“言”，则指向那些无法言说却真实存在的关怀——水流声里听见都市人的孤独低语，泡沫消散前藏着制作者凝视的温度。

在这个加速到连洗手都沦为打卡动作的时代，“沐言”不做大声宣告，亦不追逐流量喧嚣。它只以一块皂的弧度、一缕香的气息、一抹润的触感，在指尖与心尖之间架起一座微小却坚定的桥——无需言语，却完成了一场关于陪伴、尊严与温柔的契约。
